title: CBS Radio Workshop
paragraphs: CBS's mid-1950s experimental radio anthology, using drama, documentary techniques, sound, music, and literary adaptation to explore what storytelling could do in the radio medium.

CBS experimental anthology blending drama, documentary technique, literary adaptation, music and sound experimentation. Frozen GRH snapshot contains all 86 dated broadcasts in the documented 1956-57 run.

GRH documents the program through Friday experimental anthology (January 27, 1956 to October 26, 1956) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Sunday experimental anthology (November 4, 1956 to September 22, 1957) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are William N. Robson (director on 11 recordings, producer on 8 recordings, radio adaptor on 3 recordings, writer on 3 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), [[person|william-conrad|William Conrad]] (performer on 9 recordings, narrator on 5 recordings, announcer on 2 recordings, author on 1 recording, and director on 1 recording), Hugh Douglas (announcer on 10 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Ben Wright (performer on 9 recordings and author on 1 recording), Luis Van Rooten (performer on 8 recordings and narrator on 1 recording), Ralph Bell (performer on 8 recordings and narrator on 1 recording), and [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]] (performer on 9 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), [[org|org.bc515a817083485c|WGBI]] (aircheck from station), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.c02e02e51669c221|WCBS-FM]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include technology, media and modern systems, experimental radio and sound form, literary adaptation and authored texts, music and sound as narrative material, social satire and contemporary society, and science fiction and speculative futures.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Revival of the Columbia Workshop experimental tradition, Network radio experimentation during the television era, and Sound-first experimental production.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (104 shared credited people), [[show|escape|Escape]] (76 shared credited people), [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (79 shared credited people), [[show|suspense|Suspense]] (80 shared credited people), and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (52 shared credited people).
